sentences.text: 2 CORAM:
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM
ORAL ORDER

The captioned petition is filed seeking quashing of the proceedings pending in C.C.No.20625/2024 in Crime No.017/2024, for the offenses punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 506, 509 and 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
2. Today, a joint affidavit duly signed by all parties has been filed before this Court, evidencing an amicable settlement of the disputes between them.
The brother of respondent No.2/complainant is present in person before this Court.
Respondent No.2/complainant has also appeared through virtual mode.
She has been duly identified by her learned counsel on record as well as by her brother present in Court.

3. Upon specific query by this Court, respondent No.2/complainant has unequivocally stated that the matrimonial dispute between her and petitioner No.1, as NC: 2025:KHC:30839 HC-KAR well as the related grievances involving petitioner Nos.2 and 3 (her in-laws), has been resolved amicably in terms of a settlement recorded in M.C. No.4048/2025 on the file of the competent Family Court.
She further acknowledges that, under the terms of the settlement, she had already received a sum of Rs.7,00,000/- (Rupees Seven Lakhs Only) by way of demand draft.
4. It is placed on record that, in further performance of the settlement terms, the balance sum of Rs.3,00,000/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Only) has been paid today by way of demand draft.
The said demand draft has been handed over by the learned counsel for the petitioners to the brother of respondent No.2 in open Court, and the receipt thereof has been duly acknowledged.

5. In view of the above developments, it is manifest that the dispute between the parties is purely matrimonial in nature and has arisen out of domestic NC: 2025:KHC:30839 HC-KAR discord between husband and wife, also involving the in- laws.

Now that the wife--respondent No.2 herein has voluntarily entered into a lawful settlement without any coercion or undue influence, and has specifically tendered her no objection to the quashing of the proceedings, there remains no impediment in allowing the parties to compound the offences.

6. Having regard to the nature of the dispute, the settlement arrived at, and the fact that the complainant herself has expressed no desire to pursue the matter further, this Court is of the considered opinion that the continuation of the criminal proceedings would be an abuse of the process of law and would not serve the ends of justice.
Accordingly, the joint affidavit filed by the parties is taken on record.
Permission is accorded to the parties to compound the offences in view of the lawful settlement placed before this Court.
NC: 2025:KHC:30839 HC-KAR 7.

In view of the joint affidavit, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
